title: Tacenta test-vector file
description: A set of known-answer or conformance vectors for one algorithm or protocol component. Primitive vectors come from public standards; protocol vectors are generated from the Lean model. Byte strings are lowercase hex.

algorithm.description: The primitive or protocol component under test, e.g. hkdf-sha256 or double-ratchet.

source.description: Where the answers come from: a standards reference for primitive vectors, or the model revision that generated protocol vectors.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the file.

result.description: Whether the operation is expected to succeed. A valid vector carries output or fields. An invalid vector carries neither, and its input must be refused (in the three decoder files under vectors/malformed-input/, as a decode failure; in the persisted-state files, with the refusal it names), with one exception: in vectors/post-quantum/erasure-decode.json, invalid means that the decoder, offered the listed codewords, holds no value, which is not a refusal (tacenta-test-vectors/README.md, Vector layouts).

inputs.description: Named inputs, each a lowercase hex string. Where a file's inputs are the fields of a format a protocol page specifies, each input is that field's encoded bytes, and the page says where an input's name differs from its field's. For the composite header (vectors/serialization/message-encoding.json and vectors/post-quantum/composite.json), tacenta-spec/protocol/message-format.md, Ratchet message, says that the input chunk_data is the field chunk, and that chunk_present, chunk_index and chunk_data together encode one optional codeword: when chunk_present is 00, the other two are its all-zero padding. The inputs and outputs of the erasure-code, persistence, protobuf and AEAD files, and of the three decoder files under vectors/malformed-input/, are laid out in tacenta-test-vectors/README.md, Vector layouts. In each decoder file the one input, encoding, is the bytes handed to the decoder, whole: in composite-header-decode.json a 102-byte composite header and nothing after it, in prekey-bundle-decode.json a whole prekey bundle, and in initial-message-decode.json a whole initial message. In the AEAD files (vectors/aead/), the input ad is what message-format.md, Authenticated encryption, calls AD: the whole associated data given to HMAC-SHA256, which for a ratchet message is already CONCAT(ad, header). A runner does not apply CONCAT to it.

output.description: Expected output for a valid vector, lowercase hex. For the files tacenta-test-vectors/README.md, Vector layouts, describes, that section says what the output is.

refusal.description: Carried only by an invalid vector. Every invalid vector in vectors/persistence/ carries one except the erasure coders': ratchet-state, sparse-ratchet-state, triple-ratchet-state, braid-state, prekey-store-state and session-state. For stored bytes offered to a reader: which of the refusals tacenta-spec/protocol/session-persistence.md, Rejection, names the reader gives the input. wrong-version is an unrecognised version. short-or-malformed is everything else a reader refuses, a state its semantic rules exclude included, and is what every format but the session gives for those. inconsistent is the session's alone: Rejection distinguishes it from malformed because a stored session that is well-formed and canonical but cannot go on is the one case a storage layer could plausibly have written itself, so the session's semantic rules carry it and its field-by-field refusals do not. non-canonical is named by that section too and carried by no vector: a reader that accepts only canonical encodings cannot be offered one, which Model.PersistedState.SessionState's ofBytes_ok proves for the model's reader. For operations whose last step is refused: counter-exhaustion, the refusal ratchet.md (Sending and receiving) and sparse-pq-ratchet.md (Sending, Receiving) give a step past a counter's ceiling (ChainExhausted).

fields.description: For a valid vector of a decoder: the named values the input decodes to, each a lowercase hex string, an integer as its big-endian bytes. Carried instead of output. A value the decoder reports absent is left out, and a runner must check that the names match as well as the values. The protobuf files (vectors/protobuf/) spell field names in snake_case where tacenta-spec/protocol/protobuf-profile.md spells them in camelCase: ratchet_key is ratchetKey, previous_counter is previousCounter, prekey_id is prekeyId, base_key is baseKey, identity_key is identityKey, registration_id is registrationId, signed_prekey_id is signedPrekeyId, and pq_prekey_id is pqPrekeyId. counter, ciphertext, pq, message and kem are spelled the same in both. Names are compared in the vectors' spelling.
